newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: BROKERS SAY ARBED A "BUY" AFTER CSI DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BROKERS SAY ARBED A "BUY" AFTER CSI DEAL.

text.p: Shares in Luxembourg steel maker Arbed, which have lagged the European sector for months, now look poised for a rebound after the group secured a deal last week to buy part of Spanish steel firm CSI, analysts said.
"Having underperformed for nearly two years, Arbed shares may be turning a corner," Salomon Brothers in London said in a research note in which it upgraded its recommendation on the stock to "buy".
"The deal will add value to earnings in the short run and enterprise value further out," it said.
An analyst at another London house, which had a neutral rating on steels as a whole, said Arbed should outperform.
"Arbed has been left behind and the stock is undervalued relative to its fundamentals," he said. "(The CSI partnership) gives them a lot of options."

The CSI deal, which will give Arbed valuable access to the Spanish car market, centres around a share swap and involves only a small cash outlay for Arbed which the company says will be between 25 and 30 billion pesetas.

Arbed says it has not yet decided what means it will use to finance the deal, though finding cash would not be a problem. At the same time, it notes, its balance sheet will be strengthened by the deal.
Analysts said the low cash element means Arbed's already high gearing, which one put at 82 pecent, would not be stretched.

Salomon Brothers expected Arbed's gearing to decline somewhat although it would probably stay in the 75 to 80 percent range. The broker forecast that, after the transaction, Arbed's net debt would stand at 88.6 billion francs compared to 81.6 billion at the end of 1996.

Betty Pestiaux, chief analyst at Belgium's Banque Bruxelles Lambert, said while Arbed's main problem was its debt, this would not be weighed down by the first stages of the deal as CSI would effectively be paying for itself.

Under the deal, Arbed will acquire the 35 percent in CSI - Corporacion Siderurgica Integral - by subscribing to a capital increase in CSI amounting to 31 billion Luxembourg francs. It will also get warrants to acquire a further 15 percent of CSI.
In return, CSI will pay 36.4 billion pesetas for 9.5 percent of Arbed in the form of 930,000 newly created Arbed shares.
This values the Arbed shares at about 9,570 francs each, twice the market price on the Brussels bourse.

"Although we would not regard this astonishing valuation as a target price, this clear indication of what the company thinks it is worth should at least support Arbed's (share) price," Belgium's Generale Bank said in an investor note.
CSI will also buy 25 percent stakes in Arbed companies Sidstahl and Europrofil for an estimated 22 billion pesetas, and acquire other Arbed participations for 40.3 billion pesetas.
Arbed's plan for CSI includes further investment put at over 30 billion francs over the longer term.
"CSI is a profitable company with potential for significant value growth. Arbed will benefit from this even though synergies are not available early," Salomon Brothers said.
"Since CSI is more profitable than Arbed, and the implied value of CSI's participation exceeds Arbed's likely cash payment on acquisition, we believe this deal will enhance earnings."
The broker said a potential 1998 price to earnings ratio of 7.6 made the share appear undervalued.
"While we think some caution is appropriate, we believe the shares will outperform as the impact of the deal comes to be understood," it added.

Arbed shares, already boosted by a positive 1997 outlook for the steel industry published by the European Commission, showed little reaction when the news of the CSI deal was first announced last week.
Dealers said there had been some initial concern about the dilution effect of the deal on Arbed earnings.
The shares rose from 4,295 francs on July 24, the day before the Commission report, to reach 4,565 in the middle of last week, then dipped again.
By midsession on Tuesday they stood 110 francs higher at 4,590, bucking a weaker Brussels market trend.
